slides.title: Congruence Proofs
slides.html:
Congruence Proofs

I can write a proof using SAS or ASA.

geo.title: Congruence Proofs
geo.target: I can write a proof using SAS or ASA.

slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Proof-strip puzzle: each pair gets a cut-up proof (statements and reasons on separate strips) and rebuilds it. One strip is circular and must be thrown out.

  • I can plan a congruence proof in four moves: mark the givens, find the hidden equal parts (vertical angles, shared side), choose SAS or ASA, then conclude.
  • I can spot a circular step, one that uses the goal as a reason, and replace it.

geo.body:
Proof-strip puzzle: each pair gets a cut-up proof (statements and reasons on separate strips) and rebuilds it. One strip is circular and must be thrown out.

  • I can plan a congruence proof in four moves: mark the givens, find the hidden equal parts (vertical angles, shared side), choose SAS or ASA, then conclude.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: A proof plan has four moves. 1. Mark the givens on the figure. 2. Find the two triangles and write the match in order. 3. Collect three pairs of equal parts and name the test. 4. State the congruence, then use it.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
SAS proof with a shared midpoint (original, in the style of Jacobs 4.4).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
AB and CD cross at M. M is the midpoint of AB and of CD.Given.
AM = BM and CM = DM.Definition of midpoint.
Angle AMC ≅ angle BMD.Vertical angles.
Triangle AMC ≅ triangle BMD.SAS. A matches B, M matches M, C matches D.
AC = BD and angle ACM ≅ angle BDM.CPCTC.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
ASA proof with angle bisectors (original).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
AB bisects angle CAD and angle CBD. C and D are on opposite sides of AB.Given.
Angle CAB ≅ angle DAB and angle CBA ≅ angle DBA.Definition of angle bisector.
AB = AB.A segment equals itself.
Triangle CAB ≅ triangle DAB.ASA.
AC = AD and BC = BD.CPCTC. We did not assume any kite facts.

steps.step: AB bisects angle CAD and angle CBD. C and D are on opposite sides of AB.
Angle CAB ≅ angle DAB and angle CBA ≅ angle DBA.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan uses AC = AD to prove AC = AD.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

A proof uses AC = AD to prove AC = AD. That is going in a circle. Delete the line and start from the givens.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
In Worked example 1, AM = 7 and CM = 4. Find BM and DM.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

BM = 7 and DM = 4, because M is the midpoint.

Reveal second check

So AB = 14 and CD = 8, each split in half.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
In Worked example 1, AC = 3x - 1 and BD = 14. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

The triangles are congruent, so 3x - 1 = 14 and x = 5.

Reveal second check

Plug in: 15 - 1 = 14.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
In Worked example 2, can AC = AD be your first reason?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. That is what you are trying to prove. Start with the two bisected angle pairs and AB = AB.

Reveal second check

Without that line, the ASA facts are still all there.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html:
Two triangles share side XY. What property gives you XY = XY in a proof?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

The reflexive property of equality.

Reveal second check

Name the givens and the theorem or definition used.
